newsitem.title: USA: Crews report progress battling major U.S. wildfires.
newsitem.headline: Crews report progress battling major U.S. wildfires.

text.p: More than 800 firefighters struggled Sunday to dig fire lines in steep terrain around a major Montana blaze that has destroyed 34 homes and threatened a dozen more, officials said.

The Shepard Mountain fire, burning in the Custer National Forest of southern Montana, flared up last week, leaving a trail of destroyed summer homes. Thirty-four homes and three outbuildings were lost.
The lightning-sparked fire, which was burning about 20 miles west of the town of Red Lodge, had consumed 12,800 acres by Sunday, little changed from Saturday.

Firefighters said they were gaining ground on the blaze, aided by calmer winds. Officials said they were using seven airplanes and eight helicopters to drop retardant and water on the fire's hot spots.
About 60 residents of a subdivision hard hit by the fire should be allowed to return to visit their property on Monday to begin to assess the damage, officials said.
"If the weather holds, we're going to be able to coral this thing," fire information officer Bill Pidanick said. "The one thing that could really hurt us now is if we get heavy wind again."
Across the West, firefighters said they were making good progress battling major forest fires.

In southern California, firefighters said they would soon fully contain a 600 acre blaze in the Angeles National Forest. The fire was threatening an electric power line and a power facility, the National Interagency Fire Centre said.

In Wyoming, higher humidity and decreasing winds helped firefighters gain ground on two major blazes. In Oregon, the fire activity continued to moderate and some weary crews were being demobilized, the fire centre said.
The National Interagency Fire Centre, based in Boise, Idaho, said 7,765 firefighters were battling eight major fires burning on 135,915 acres in California, Idaho, Montana, Oregon and Wyoming.

A U.S. Army battalion of about 550 people, called up to aid firefighters in Oregon, will return to its base at Fort Carson, Colorado on Monday after completing mopup at the Summit Fire in Oregon. A Marine battalion from southern California will stay in Oregon until at least Wednesday.

The Western United States has been experiencing its worst fire season in 30 years, with fires spreading quickly in parched grass, brush and forest. More than 5.8 million acres have burned so far this year, compared with a five-year average of 2.1 million acres.
While progress was being made on fire lines across the West, Carol Connolly, fire information officer for the fire centre, warned: "We're not out of the woods yet. It's still really dry out there."
